extraction.name: Vibravox
extraction.description: A GDPR-compliant dataset containing audio recordings using five different body-conduction audio sensors (two in-ear microphones, two bone conduction vibration pickups, and a laryngophone) plus an airborne microphone reference. Contains 45 hours per sensor of French speech samples and physiological sounds recorded by 188 participants under different acoustic conditions imposed by a high order ambisonics 3D spatializer.
extraction.creator: Julien Hauret, Malo Olivier, Thomas Joubaud, Christophe Langrenne, Sarah Poirée, Véronique Zimpfer, and Éric Bavu
extraction.citeAs: Hauret, J., Olivier, M., Joubaud, T., Langrenne, C., Poirée, S., Zimpfer, V., & Bavu, É. (2024). Vibravox: A Dataset of French Speech Captured with Body-conduction Audio Sensors. Submitted to Elsevier Speech Communication on August 20, 2024 - Revision submitted on March 29, 2025. arXiv:2407.11828v4 [eess.AS].
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Audio recordings were obtained from sensors worn by participants during four consecutive recording steps: speech-clean (15 minutes of reading sentences), speechless-noisy (2 minutes 24 seconds of silence in noisy environment), speechless-clean (54 seconds of silence in quiet), and speech-noisy (54 seconds of reading in noisy environment). Recordings were made using a Zoom F8n field recorder at 48 kHz sampling rate and 32-bit resolution with a 20 Hz high-pass filter applied to each channel.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Text for participant readings originated from the French Wikipedia subset of Common Voice. Noise excerpts were sourced from AudioSet with focus on noise classes relevant to BCMs applications (battlefield and industrial environments), plus in-house recordings of concerts and street events in 3rd and 5th order ambisonics.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Three automatic filters were applied to remove utterances with deficiencies: (1) PER filter discarding samples where Phoneme Error Rate > 10%, (2) SNR filter verifying speech-to-silence energy ratio > 1.5 dB, and (3) sensitivity drift filter checking that speech level exceeds silence level. Voice Activity Detection timestamps were extended by 0.6 seconds on both sides, with 15 ms trimming when exceeding audio boundaries. Text normalization included lowercasing and removing punctuation except apostrophes.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Phonetic transcriptions were generated using the International Phonetic Alphabet (IPA) with 33 French phonemes using the text phonemizer of the CoML lab. Manual phonetic transcription was performed for words not recognized by the phonemizer. Textual filters excluded proper names (retaining only common first names, French town/region names, and country names), numbers, Greek letters, mathematical symbols, and syntactic errors.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: whisper-timestamped model (based on Whisper) for speech-to-text and word timestamp prediction using dynamic time warping on cross-attention weights; CoML lab text phonemizer for phonetic transcription
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Gender information was collected and balanced during participant recruitment. The dataset contains voice recordings which are biometric data.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: In some cases, such as when a participant's ear canal was too small for the rigid in-ear microphone to achieve proper acoustic sealing, automatic filters were not triggered. The dataset is limited to French language. Some in-ear microphones were affected by acoustic sealing issues for certain ear canal anatomies that do not fit the sensor properly.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, and Validation for speech enhancement (bandwidth extension), speech recognition, and speaker verification tasks. The dataset is designed for developing robust communication systems in noisy environments, particularly for military operations and industrial settings. The speechless-clean subset can be used for heart rate tracking and analyzing noise properties of sensors.

description.evidence: Vibravox is a dataset compliant with the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) containing audio recordings using five different body-conduction audio sensors: two in-ear microphones, two bone conduction vibration pickups, and a laryngophone. The dataset also includes audio data from an airbome microphone used as a reference. The Vibravox corpus contains 45 hours per sensor of speech samples and physiological sounds recorded by 188 participants under different acoustic conditions imposed by a high order ambisonics 3D spatializer.
